text:
The diff does not match the ticket: the ticket asks for jumbo frames, but the diff lowers the MTU from 1500 to 1400 on both ends of the AAR-SLC link. The tests below verify the change as written, so they will flag this mismatch by failing the jumbo-frame (9000) probe and the 1500-byte probe.

```json
{"tests": [
  {"t":"mtu","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","size":9000,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"noc1","dst":"ext-dns1","size":9000,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"noc1","dst":"ext-dns1","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"c2-host","dst":"noc1","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"AAR","b":"SLC","expect":"up"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"AAR","prefix":"10.0.3.28/30","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"SLC","prefix":"10.0.3.28/30","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"ext-dns1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"ext-dns2","svc":"icmp","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"noc2","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noclab1","dst":"noclab2","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"conv","a":"AAR","b":"SLC","max_s":3},
  {"t":"load","a":"AAR","b":"SLC","max_pct":90}
]}
```

Notes for the reviewer:
- The 9000-byte probes are expected to fail on this diff. If they do, either the diff is wrong (it should raise the MTU, e.g. to 9000, on both ends) or the ticket is wrong. Do not approve until this is resolved.
- The 1500-byte probes are expected to fail too, since the link MTU is now 1400. That would break standard-size DF traffic across this link for any flow that traverses it.
- The `adj` test is a regression check: OSPF adjacencies can drop on an MTU mismatch, and the two ends match here (1400/1400), so it should stay up.
- Even if the diff is corrected to 9000, every other device on the path would also need a matching MTU for end-to-end jumbo frames. Hosts are all at 1500, so true end-to-end jumbo would not work without further changes.
